text:
Mark Jankowski has eight goals in 16 games, which is how a journeyman ends up in headlines. He's the one stepping up for Jordan Staal, as The Athletic framed it, with "Conn Smythe shoes to fill," and Carolina has given him more ice, up more than two minutes a night over his last ten.

Enjoy it, but know what it is. He's shooting 27%, against 17% last season, on 5.1 expected goals. The chances are real (that's why the minutes keep coming); the finishing rate almost never holds. The more durable skill is the defensive one: Evolving-Hockey had him in the 92nd percentile for taking chances away last season, and he was better than his goals then too.

At 32, after stops in Calgary, Pittsburgh, Buffalo and Nashville, he has a Cup ring from last spring and the best stretch of his career. Our range has him at 17 to 29 goals, a fine season even after the cooling.
